basedOn: Standard GI physiology: microbial fermentation of fiber and resistant starch into short-chain fatty acids (butyrate, propionate, acetate), colonocyte fuelling, and water/electrolyte reclamation over ~12-40 h. Teaching averages.
sources: NIDDK - Your Digestive System & How It Works: https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/digestive-system-how-it-works
Hall & Hall, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. - Unit XII, Gastrointestinal Physiology
Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology, 3rd ed. - The Gastrointestinal System

substrateArrival.label: Substrate arrival
substrateArrival.detail: Fiber and resistant starch that survived the small intestine arrive as microbiome fuel - not 'wasted calories' but the substrate for fermentation.

edgeCases.effect: Little fermentable substrate -> thin SCFA yield; the microbiome is under-fed this meal.
edgeCases.note: Teaching pattern across a low-fiber dietary pattern, not one meal.

fermentation.label: Microbial fermentation
fermentation.detail: Given enough substrate, gut bacteria ferment fiber into short-chain fatty acids (butyrate, propionate, acetate) that feed the colonocytes and signal systemically.

scfaRich.label: SCFA-rich fermentation
scfaRich.detail: Butyrate fuels colonocytes; propionate/acetate reach the liver and periphery - gut-barrier and immune teaching narrative.

scfaLean.label: SCFA-lean fermentation
scfaLean.detail: Low substrate means little fermentation and a thinner SCFA yield - the cost of a low-fiber pattern, framed honestly, not as calorie waste.

reclaim.label: Water & electrolyte reclamation
reclaim.detail: The colon reclaims water and electrolytes and compacts the residue - the journey's final metering step (~12-40 h total).
